description: Source registry for the AI-Powered Computer Engineering Student Advisor knowledge base. Sources will be added during the source collection stage.

source_id.description: Unique identifier for the source, for example src_001.

title.description: Title of the document, page, report, article, or resource.

source_name.description: Name of the organization, website, institution, publisher, or document owner.

source_type.description: Type of source, such as official_department_page, curriculum_document, academic_paper, professional_organization, educational_website, career_resource, industry_report, or official_documentation.

url.description: Original URL for web sources. Leave empty for offline files.

publication_date.description: Publication or last-updated date in YYYY-MM-DD format when known.

date_accessed.description: Date the source was collected or reviewed in YYYY-MM-DD format.

language.description: Source language, for example English or Turkish.

reliability_note.description: Short note explaining why the source is considered reliable or what limitations it has.

raw_file_path.description: Local path to the stored raw copy under knowledge_base/raw when available.

notes.description: Extra notes about scope, useful sections, duplication, or preprocessing decisions.

sources.title: About the Department | MF-Bilgisayar Mühendisliği (İngilizce)
sources.source_name: OSTIM Technical University - Department of Computer Engineering (English)
sources.reliability_note: Official OSTIM Technical University Computer Engineering department page. It directly describes the department aim, program design, and hardware/software/system focus.
sources.notes: Supports questions about what Computer Engineering is, what students study, hardware/software balance, and the department's educational purpose. Secondary categories: curriculum, career_opportunities, skills_and_technologies.

sources.title: Mission and Vission | MF-Bilgisayar Mühendisliği (İngilizce)
sources.source_name: OSTIM Technical University - Department of Computer Engineering (English)
sources.reliability_note: Official department mission and vision page from OSTIM Technical University. It is reliable for the department's stated educational goals and institutional direction.
sources.notes: Supports questions about program objectives, academic structure, research orientation, industry connection, and the department's future-technology focus. Secondary categories: future_technologies, skills_and_technologies, career_opportunities.

sources.title: Curriculum | MF-Bilgisayar Mühendisliği (İngilizce)
sources.source_name: OSTIM Technical University - Department of Computer Engineering (English)
sources.reliability_note: Official OSTIM Technical University Computer Engineering curriculum page. It lists the current curriculum after 2024-2025, semesters, course codes, course names, credits, ECTS values, and prerequisites.
sources.notes: Supports questions about curriculum, mathematics load, programming courses, hardware/software balance, technical electives, workplace education, and graduation project structure. Secondary categories: programming, mathematics, internships, skills_and_technologies, artificial_intelligence, cybersecurity, entrepreneurship.

sources.title: Course Contents | MF-Bilgisayar Mühendisliği (İngilizce)
sources.source_name: OSTIM Technical University - Department of Computer Engineering (English)
sources.reliability_note: Official department course contents page. It provides course-level descriptions for programming, mathematics, software engineering, workplace experience, trends, and graduation projects.
sources.notes: Supports questions about what students study, course difficulty, programming languages, projects, internships/workplace experience, future technologies, and career preparation. Secondary categories: programming, mathematics, internships, student_life, future_technologies, skills_and_technologies.

sources.title: Our Difference | MF-Bilgisayar Mühendisliği (İngilizce)
sources.source_name: OSTIM Technical University - Department of Computer Engineering (English)
sources.reliability_note: Official department page explaining OSTIM Technical University's applied education model, workplace applications, entrepreneurship scorecard, and educational philosophy.
sources.notes: Supports questions about student opportunities, practical training, industry connection, entrepreneurship, workplace learning, and why the program may be distinctive. Secondary categories: internships, entrepreneurship, career_opportunities, skills_and_technologies.

sources.title: Academic Staff
sources.source_name: OSTIM Technical University - Department of Computer Engineering (English)
sources.reliability_note: Official department academic staff page. It identifies faculty members, roles, contact information, offices, and research fields.
sources.notes: Supports questions about academic structure, faculty expertise, AI, NLP, software engineering, cybersecurity, networks, databases, and research exposure. Secondary categories: artificial_intelligence, cybersecurity, graduate_studies, specializations.

sources.title: Workplace Documents | MF-Bilgisayar Mühendisliği (İngilizce)
sources.source_name: OSTIM Technical University - Department of Computer Engineering (English)
sources.reliability_note: Official department page listing workplace-related documents, including evaluation reports, daily attendance sheet, and report book links.
sources.notes: Supports questions about workplace education documentation and internship/workplace experience requirements. Secondary categories: curriculum, employment, student_life.

sources.title: Research | MF-Bilgisayar Mühendisliği (İngilizce)
sources.source_name: OSTIM Technical University - Department of Computer Engineering (English)
sources.reliability_note: Official department research page. It lists research areas and publications connected with Computer Engineering faculty.
sources.notes: Supports questions about specialization areas, AI, embedded systems, software, programming languages, computer networks, NLP, big data, information security, and academic/research opportunities. Secondary categories: artificial_intelligence, cybersecurity, graduate_studies, future_technologies.

sources.title: Curricula Recommendations
sources.source_name: Association for Computing Machinery (ACM)
sources.reliability_note: Official ACM education page for computing curriculum recommendations, including computer engineering curriculum guidance.
sources.notes: Supports questions about what Computer Engineering programs should cover, how computing disciplines differ, and why curriculum design matters. Secondary categories: department_information, skills_and_technologies, specializations.

sources.title: Software Developers, Quality Assurance Analysts, and Testers
sources.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Occupational Outlook Handbook
sources.reliability_note: Official U.S. government labor profile with duties, work environment, education, pay, employment, and outlook information.
sources.notes: Supports questions about software careers, job demand, industries, internships, salary context, degree expectations, and career progression. Secondary categories: employment, salaries, internships, skills_and_technologies, graduate_studies, work_life_balance.

sources.title: Computer Hardware Engineers
sources.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Occupational Outlook Handbook
sources.reliability_note: Official U.S. government labor profile for computer hardware engineering with duties, education, skills, industries, pay, and outlook.
sources.notes: Supports questions about the hardware side of Computer Engineering, electronics/computer architecture work, programming relevance, internships, industries, and employment outlook. Secondary categories: employment, skills_and_technologies, programming, internships, salaries.

sources.title: Information Security Analysts
sources.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Occupational Outlook Handbook
sources.reliability_note: Official U.S. government labor profile for cybersecurity-related work, including duties, education, certifications, pay, employment, and outlook.
sources.notes: Supports questions about cybersecurity career paths, demand, required skills, certifications, industries, and salary context. Secondary categories: career_opportunities, employment, skills_and_technologies, salaries, specializations.

sources.title: Computer and Information Research Scientists
sources.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Occupational Outlook Handbook
sources.reliability_note: Official U.S. government labor profile describing research computing careers, graduate education expectations, duties, pay, and outlook.
sources.notes: Supports questions about whether a master's degree is necessary for research roles, graduate study value, AI/research careers, and advanced career paths. Secondary categories: artificial_intelligence, career_opportunities, employment, future_technologies, salaries.

sources.title: Computer Hardware Engineers: 17-2061.00
sources.source_name: O*NET OnLine
sources.reliability_note: O*NET is sponsored by the U.S. Department of Labor and provides structured occupational tasks, activities, skills, technology examples, and work context.
sources.notes: The page is marked Updated 2026. Supports questions about real computer hardware engineering tasks, tools, Linux, Git, programming, apprenticeship, work context, and required skills. Secondary categories: career_opportunities, employment, programming, work_life_balance.

sources.title: About Git
sources.source_name: GitHub Docs
sources.reliability_note: Official GitHub documentation explaining Git, distributed version control, collaboration, branches, and development workflow basics.
sources.notes: Supports questions about why Git and GitHub are important skills for Computer Engineering students and software teamwork. Secondary categories: programming, internships, employment.

sources.title: 2024 State of Tech Talent Report
sources.source_name: The Linux Foundation
sources.reliability_note: Linux Foundation Research report with a DOI, focused on technical hiring, upskilling, cloud/DevOps, cybersecurity, AI/ML, and open-source talent.
sources.notes: Report year is 2024. Supports questions about Linux/open-source importance, in-demand technology skills, upskilling, AI/ML, cybersecurity, cloud, and DevOps. Secondary categories: employment, future_technologies, artificial_intelligence, cybersecurity.

sources.title: The Future of Jobs Report 2025
sources.source_name: World Economic Forum
sources.reliability_note: Recognized international report analyzing job transformation, technology trends, in-demand roles, and skill changes.
sources.notes: Supports questions about whether Computer Engineering is still a good career choice, AI's labor-market impact, future technologies, and high-demand digital skills. Secondary categories: career_opportunities, employment, artificial_intelligence, skills_and_technologies.

sources.title: Students Recognize the Importance of Gaining Internship Experience
sources.source_name: National Association of Colleges and Employers (NACE)
sources.reliability_note: NACE is a professional association focused on college recruiting, internships, and career readiness; the article reports survey-based student internship findings.
sources.notes: Supports questions about internship importance, career readiness, gaining experience before graduation, and employability preparation. Secondary categories: employment, student_life, skills_and_technologies.

sources.title: Working time and work-life balance around the world
sources.source_name: International Labour Organization
sources.reliability_note: Official ILO research repository report on working time, work-life balance, flexible arrangements, and telework.
sources.notes: Report metadata lists the publication year as 2022. Supports general questions about work-life balance, remote/flexible work, and working-time concerns. Secondary categories: remote_work, employment.

sources.title: Business Guide
sources.source_name: U.S. Small Business Administration
sources.reliability_note: Official U.S. government small-business guidance covering planning, launching, managing, growing a business, training, and counseling resources.
sources.notes: Supports questions about whether Computer Engineering graduates can become entrepreneurs, how technical founders can plan a business, and what support resources exist. Secondary categories: career_opportunities, skills_and_technologies.

sources.title: Higher Education Employment Indicators, 2025
sources.source_name: Turkish Statistical Institute (TURKSTAT / TÜİK)
sources.reliability_note: Official TURKSTAT press release using administrative registers matched in the Education-Labour Force Database.
sources.notes: Turkey-specific. Supports graduate employment, first-job duration, field alignment, and monthly average earnings indicators by higher-education field/programme. Measurement year: 2025. Important limitation: public page gives field-level ICT indicators and ranked earnings, not a full Computer Engineering salary table in the inspected text. Secondary categories: salaries, graduate_studies, career_opportunities.

sources.title: Labour Force Statistics, 2025
sources.source_name: Turkish Statistical Institute (TURKSTAT / TÜİK)
sources.reliability_note: Official TURKSTAT annual labor-force statistics for Türkiye.
sources.notes: Turkey-specific. Supports general labor-market context such as employment, unemployment, labor-force participation, youth unemployment, and sector distribution. Measurement year: 2025. Important limitation: not specific to Computer Engineering or ICT occupations.

sources.title: Labour Cost Statistics, 2024
sources.source_name: Turkish Statistical Institute (TURKSTAT / TÜİK)
sources.reliability_note: Official TURKSTAT labor-cost statistics by economic activity.
sources.notes: Turkey-specific salary/labor-cost evidence. Measurement year: 2024. Covers monthly average labor cost, gross wage, and gross earnings by sector, including Information and Communication. Currency: TRY. Important limitation: sector-level labor cost is not the same as an individual Computer Engineering salary. Secondary categories: employment.

sources.title: Structure of Earnings Statistics, 2022
sources.source_name: Turkish Statistical Institute (TURKSTAT / TÜİK)
sources.reliability_note: Official TURKSTAT earnings statistics using administrative register data, with methodology and data-source notes.
sources.notes: Turkey-specific salary evidence. Reference year: 2022. Covers monthly and annual gross wages/earnings by education level, economic activity, and occupation group. Currency: TRY. Important limitation: authoritative but older than ideal, and not occupation-specific for Computer Engineering. Secondary categories: employment.

sources.title: ICT
sources.source_name: Presidency of the Republic of Türkiye Investment Office
sources.reliability_note: Official Türkiye Investment Office sector page summarizing ICT market size, companies, employees, R&D centers, and graduates.
sources.notes: Turkey-specific ICT sector evidence. Includes 2024 market and workforce indicators, ICT employment, R&D personnel, exports, and engineering/ICT graduate supply. Important limitation: investment-promotion page rather than a statistical microdata release. Secondary categories: career_opportunities, future_technologies, entrepreneurship.

sources.title: Turkey - Information and Communication Technology
sources.source_name: International Trade Administration, U.S. Department of Commerce
sources.reliability_note: Official U.S. government country commercial guide for Türkiye's ICT sector.
sources.notes: Turkey-specific ICT market and employment evidence. Measurement years include 2024 and 2025 projections. Supports questions about software market growth, IT employment, ICT exports, AI, cybersecurity, cloud, IoT, data centers, and 5G. Important limitation: commercial guide, not a primary Turkish statistical source. Secondary categories: career_opportunities, future_technologies, artificial_intelligence, cybersecurity, remote_work.

sources.title: TÜBİSAD 2024 Bilgi ve İletişim Teknolojileri Sektörü Pazar Verileri ve Trendleri Raporu
sources.source_name: TÜBİSAD Bilişim Sanayicileri Derneği
sources.reliability_note: Official TÜBİSAD report page for Türkiye ICT sector market data and trends.
sources.notes: Turkey-specific ICT sector evidence. Report year: 2024. Supports questions about technology-sector scale, market trends, and employment context. Important limitation: inspected report landing page identifies the report but exposes limited methodology text without downloading the full report. Secondary categories: career_opportunities, skills_and_technologies, future_technologies.

sources.title: Preparing for work abroad
sources.source_name: Europass, European Union
sources.reliability_note: Official Europass guidance on preparing skills, qualifications, CV documents, and recognition steps for work in Europe.
sources.notes: International-career evidence. Supports questions about working abroad, presenting qualifications, checking whether a profession is regulated, ENIC-NARIC recognition, EQF/NQF, diplomas, transcripts, and Diploma Supplement. Important limitation: EU mobility guidance, not a guarantee of employment or immigration eligibility. Secondary categories: employment, career_opportunities, graduate_studies.

sources.title: EU Blue Card
sources.source_name: European Commission - Migration and Home Affairs
sources.reliability_note: Official European Commission page explaining the EU Blue Card for highly qualified non-EU workers.
sources.notes: International-career evidence. Supports questions about working in EU countries as a highly qualified worker, job offers, qualification documents, national authority applications, and legal cautions. Important limitation: immigration rules vary by EU Member State and this source must not be used to give personalized legal advice. Secondary categories: employment, career_opportunities.

sources.title: Türkiye
sources.source_name: ENIC-NARIC Networks
sources.reliability_note: Official ENIC-NARIC country profile for Türkiye, identifying YÖK/CoHE recognition bodies, higher education structure, qualification frameworks, and Diploma Supplement information.
sources.notes: Turkey and international recognition evidence. Page states it was last updated in 2026. Supports questions about degree recognition, Turkish higher education qualifications, international study/work preparation, and graduate admissions context. Important limitation: recognition guidance is general and destination-country rules still matter. Secondary categories: employment, remote_work.

sources.title: A Skills-First Labour Market
sources.source_name: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)
sources.reliability_note: OECD report with DOI on skills-first hiring, skills recognition, labor-market transformation, career guidance, and professional development.
sources.notes: Supports questions about GPA versus skills, personal projects, professional development, skills-first hiring, career progression, lifelong learning, micro-credentials, and academic credentials. Important limitation: global/OECD evidence, not Computer Engineering-only and not Turkey-specific. Secondary categories: employment, career_opportunities, graduate_studies.

sources.title: Working anytime, anywhere: The quality of working time in the EU
sources.source_name: Eurofound
sources.reliability_note: Eurofound is an EU agency; this research report covers flexible work, telework, working-time quality, and work-life balance.
sources.notes: International remote-work and work-life balance evidence. Measurement includes EU working conditions in 2024. Supports questions about remote work benefits, risks, autonomy, overwork, and boundary blurring. Important limitation: EU-wide evidence, not Turkey-specific and not software-only. Secondary categories: remote_work, employment.

sources.title: Hiring Projections Level Off for the College Class of 2025
sources.source_name: National Association of Colleges and Employers (NACE)
sources.reliability_note: NACE article based on the Job Outlook 2025 Spring Update employer survey.
sources.notes: Supports GPA versus skills questions, entry-level hiring outlook, skills-based hiring, major relevance, and internship importance. Important limitation: U.S. employer survey, not Computer Engineering-only and not Turkey-specific. Secondary categories: career_opportunities, internships, skills_and_technologies.

sources.title: Employers Say New Grads Are Largely Prepared for Work, With Room to Improve
sources.source_name: National Association of Colleges and Employers (NACE)
sources.reliability_note: NACE article summarizing employer views from the Job Outlook 2026 Spring Update survey.
sources.notes: Supports questions about the importance of communication, teamwork, professionalism, critical thinking, internships, experiential learning, hackathons, and demonstrating skills with examples. Important limitation: general graduate hiring evidence, not Computer Engineering-specific. Secondary categories: employment, internships, student_life.

sources.title: Portfolios
sources.source_name: MIT Career Advising & Professional Development
sources.reliability_note: Official MIT career-advising resource about portfolio value and portfolio development.
sources.notes: Supports questions about personal projects, portfolios, showing skills and accomplishments, graduate-school applications, and building an online professional identity. Important limitation: general portfolio guidance, not a statistical employer survey. Secondary categories: skills_and_technologies, graduate_studies, internships.

sources.title: Resumes
sources.source_name: Berkeley Career Engagement
sources.reliability_note: Official UC Berkeley career resource on resumes, project experience, volunteer experience, GPA, ATS formatting, and skill demonstration.
sources.notes: Supports questions about GPA on resumes, project experience, volunteer/unpaid work, transferable skills, and how students can demonstrate employability. Important limitation: career-advice guidance, not a universal employer rule. Secondary categories: skills_and_technologies, internships, student_life.

sources.title: Intern Hiring Is Stable for 2024
sources.source_name: National Association of Colleges and Employers (NACE)
sources.reliability_note: NACE article based on the 2024 Internship & Co-op Report employer survey.
sources.notes: Supports questions about internship demand, how employers source interns, selection criteria, previous internship experience, competencies, career fairs, and hybrid internships. Important limitation: U.S. survey and not Computer Engineering-only. Secondary categories: employment, skills_and_technologies, remote_work.

sources.title: Programming/software development
sources.source_name: SFIA Foundation
sources.reliability_note: Official SFIA 9 skill page from the SFIA Foundation, a global skills and competency framework for digital work.
sources.notes: SFIA 9 was published in October 2024. Supports career progression questions by describing increasing programming/software-development responsibility levels without imposing a universal years-to-senior timeline. Secondary categories: skills_and_technologies, programming, employment.

sources.title: Which Introductory Course Should I Take?
sources.source_name: Brown University Department of Computer Science
sources.reliability_note: Official Brown CS advising page explaining introductory course pathways, prior programming assumptions, and beginner course options.
sources.notes: Supports beginner and late-start concerns, including whether prior programming experience is required and how different introductory pathways can still prepare students for later courses. Important limitation: institution-specific course advice. Secondary categories: mathematics, student_life, common_misconceptions.

sources.title: NCWIT Scorecard: The Status of Women's Participation in Computing
sources.source_name: National Center for Women & Information Technology (NCWIT)
sources.reliability_note: NCWIT data resource with downloadable charts and datasets on participation in computing by gender, race, ethnicity, education, and workforce indicators.
sources.notes: Supports questions about whether women can have successful computing careers and helps counter stereotype-based assumptions with participation data. Important limitation: mainly U.S.-focused participation data. Secondary categories: employment, student_life.

sources.title: Engagement Practices Framework: Address Misconceptions About the Field of CS
sources.source_name: National Center for Women & Information Technology (NCWIT)
sources.reliability_note: NCWIT guidance resource for educators/advisors on addressing narrow ideas about computing work, who belongs in computing, and the diversity of computing careers.
sources.notes: Supports misconception questions about computing being only for one type of person, only solitary work, or only narrow technical tasks. Important limitation: guidance resource rather than labor-market statistics. Secondary categories: student_life, career_opportunities.

sources.title: Curricular Guidance
sources.source_name: ACM Committee for Computing Education in Community Colleges
sources.reliability_note: Official ACM CCECC guidance explaining computing sub-disciplines and educational/career-program pathways.
sources.notes: Supports misconceptions about Computer Engineering being only software or only hardware by defining Computer Engineering as processor-based systems involving hardware, software, and communications. Secondary categories: department_information, curriculum, career_opportunities, graduate_studies.

sources.title: Subdisciplines
sources.source_name: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering
sources.reliability_note: Official university ECE page listing Computer Engineering focus areas and noting that student interests may combine multiple areas.
sources.notes: Supports specialization-choice questions across hardware systems, cyberphysical systems, theory, security, networking, mobile/distributed computing, big data, AI, robotics, and cybernetics. Important limitation: institution-specific advising structure. Secondary categories: artificial_intelligence, cybersecurity, future_technologies, curriculum.

sources.title: Prepare for graduate & professional school
sources.source_name: MIT Career Advising & Professional Development
sources.reliability_note: Official MIT career-advising resource for deciding whether graduate school fits a student's career plan, preparation, experience, and degree options.
sources.notes: Supports questions about whether a master's degree is necessary, when graduate school may be useful, research versus professional degrees, academic preparation, GPA, internships, research, and self-assessment. Important limitation: general graduate-school advising, not Computer Engineering-only. Secondary categories: employment, career_opportunities, skills_and_technologies.

sources.title: Skills for the digital age
sources.source_name: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)
sources.reliability_note: OECD Digital Economy Outlook chapter on digital skills, ICT specialist demand, job vacancies, wages as shortage signals, and AI-related skill changes.
sources.notes: Addresses Turkey ICT/software hiring evidence and AI skill demand. Geographic scope: OECD/international with Türkiye indicator. Notes that ICT specialists accounted for 1.4% of jobs in Türkiye in 2021-22 and discusses ICT vacancies, software engineers, AI skills, and wage-shortage interpretation. Secondary categories: employment, salaries, artificial_intelligence, future_technologies.

sources.title: OECD Economic Surveys: Türkiye 2025
sources.source_name: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)
sources.reliability_note: OECD country economic survey for Türkiye, including digital skills, ICT specialist shortages, graduate skill matching, lifelong learning, migration, and AI talent context.
sources.notes: Addresses Turkey ICT hiring evidence and international careers. Geographic scope: Türkiye. Supports questions about demand for ICT graduates, Turkey's digital-skills gap, lifelong learning, and high-skilled migration. Important limitation: macroeconomic/country evidence, not OSTIM-specific employment outcomes. Secondary categories: career_opportunities, graduate_studies, remote_work, artificial_intelligence.

sources.title: Education GPS - Türkiye - Overview of the education system (EAG 2025)
sources.source_name: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)
sources.reliability_note: OECD Education GPS country profile for Türkiye using Education at a Glance indicators.
sources.notes: Addresses Turkey graduate employment and women/ICT participation gaps. Geographic scope: Türkiye. Includes 2023 ICT graduate/new entrant indicators and 2024 employment outcomes by education level and gender. Important limitation: ICT field-level and education-system evidence, not Computer Engineering-only. Secondary categories: employment, common_misconceptions, salaries.

sources.title: Employed information and communications technology (ICT) specialists by sex
sources.source_name: European Institute for Gender Equality / Eurostat
sources.reliability_note: EIGE data viewer exposing Eurostat ICT specialist employment by sex, with Türkiye included among geographic regions.
sources.notes: Addresses women in computing/ICT for Türkiye. Geographic scope: EU/Europe plus Türkiye. Measures employed ICT specialists by sex and year in comparable percentages and thousand persons. Important limitation: ICT specialists broadly, not Computer Engineering students/graduates only. Secondary categories: employment, skills_and_technologies.

sources.title: Work | 2024 Stack Overflow Developer Survey
sources.source_name: Stack Overflow
sources.reliability_note: Large annual developer survey section covering employment status, work environment, salary by developer type, technology purchasing, and coding outside work.
sources.notes: Addresses remote/hybrid work, developer salary context, specialization salary caution, professional development, and coding outside work. Geographic scope: global developer respondents, with some top-country breakdowns. Important limitation: self-selected survey and not Turkey-specific; salary data should not be used as Turkish salary evidence. Secondary categories: salaries, employment, work_life_balance, skills_and_technologies.

sources.title: Professional Developers | 2024 Stack Overflow Developer Survey
sources.source_name: Stack Overflow
sources.reliability_note: Large annual developer survey section covering professional developer productivity, developer experience, frustrations, work context, and job satisfaction.
sources.notes: Addresses software/computing workload, frustration, stress-adjacent work factors, technical debt, knowledge silos, satisfaction, and time spent finding answers. Geographic scope: global developer respondents. Important limitation: self-selected survey; not a clinical stress/burnout study and not Turkey-specific. Secondary categories: employment, skills_and_technologies, career_opportunities.

sources.title: State of Developer Ecosystem Report 2024
sources.source_name: JetBrains
sources.reliability_note: JetBrains annual developer ecosystem survey based on 23,262 developers after data cleaning, with methodology and raw data access.
sources.notes: Addresses technologies, programming languages, AI tool use, developer workload, career transitions, job-market perceptions, team size, salary by region/language, and work challenges. Geographic scope: global developer respondents. Important limitation: industry survey with likely respondent bias; salary figures are global/region-level and not Turkey CENG salary evidence. Secondary categories: employment, salaries, artificial_intelligence, work_life_balance, programming.

sources.title: DORA Accelerate State of DevOps 2024 Report
sources.source_name: DORA, Google
sources.reliability_note: Google/DORA software engineering research report with authors listed, based on a long-running DevOps research program and global technology professionals.
sources.notes: Addresses AI impact on software development, platform engineering, productivity, team practices, and changing software engineering work. Geographic scope: global. Important limitation: software/DevOps teams, not Computer Engineering students specifically. Secondary categories: skills_and_technologies, future_technologies, work_life_balance.

sources.title: How Gen AI Affects the Value of Development Work
sources.source_name: DORA, Google
sources.reliability_note: Google/DORA research report based on interviews with professional developers about generative AI and perceived value of development work.
sources.notes: Addresses AI augmentation and how generative AI changes developer work value. Geographic scope: professional developer evidence, not Turkey-specific. Important limitation: qualitative interview report with 10 interviews; should complement broader AI labor sources, not stand alone. Secondary categories: future_technologies, work_life_balance, skills_and_technologies.

sources.title: Study Demands-Resources Theory: Understanding Student Well-Being in Higher Education
sources.source_name: Educational Psychology Review / Springer Nature
sources.reliability_note: Peer-reviewed open-access review article on study demands, resources, burnout, engagement, and student outcomes in higher education.
sources.notes: Addresses student workload, stress, burnout, engagement, support resources, and study-life balance. Geographic scope: higher education generally. Important limitation: not Computer Engineering-specific and does not provide weekly study-hour estimates. Secondary categories: work_life_balance, mathematics, common_misconceptions.

sources.title: Investigating Academic Confidence, Workload Stress, and Performance in a BlendFlex Computer Science Course
sources.source_name: ACM ITiCSE 2024
sources.reliability_note: Peer-reviewed ACM computing education paper studying academic confidence, workload stress, modality, performance, and survey/academic records in an introductory CS course.
sources.notes: Addresses computing-specific workload stress and student success concerns. Geographic scope: one U.S. university course with 412 students. Important limitation: course-specific and not Computer Engineering-wide. Secondary categories: programming, mathematics, work_life_balance.

sources.title: How Beginning Programmers and Code LLMs (Mis)read Each Other
sources.source_name: ACM CHI 2024
sources.reliability_note: Peer-reviewed ACM CHI 2024 paper examining beginning programmers, prior programming experience, math-course background, and interactions with code LLMs.
sources.notes: Addresses beginner programming and math misconception evidence. Geographic scope: selective U.S. institutions. Important limitation: specific task context with code LLMs; should not be generalized into a claim that math never matters. Secondary categories: mathematics, common_misconceptions, artificial_intelligence.

sources.title: Legislation | Ostim Teknik Üniversitesi Web sitesi
sources.source_name: OSTIM Technical University
sources.reliability_note: Official OSTIM Technical University legislation index. It is reliable for identifying university regulations and directives that apply to students.
sources.notes: Addresses OSTIM-specific academic regulations, examination rules, directives, and relevant student procedures. Secondary categories: curriculum, student_life.

sources.title: OSTIM Technical University Undergraduate Education and Examination Regulation
sources.source_name: OSTIM Technical University
sources.reliability_note: Official OSTIM Technical University undergraduate education and examination regulation document. It is authoritative for university-level registration, course load, assessment, and graduation rules.
sources.notes: Addresses OSTIM-specific registration, course enrollment, exams, grading, attendance-related procedures where present, academic standing, and graduation conditions. Secondary categories: curriculum, department_information.

sources.title: Student Affairs Main Page
